title: Batnit
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman cites Peah 8:5 for Abba Shaul ben Batnit. Hyman says that his grandson was also called Batnit: Nedarim 23a relates that Batnit son of Abba Shaul ben Batnit found an opening for the vow of R’ Shimon son of Rabbi. Hyman says it SHOULD READ R’ Shimon, as at the beginning of Jerusalem Talmud Nedarim, chapter 9, because Batnit’s grandson could not have lived in the time of Shimon son of Rabbi. Or, he says, it SHOULD READ “of the descendants of Abba Shaul ben Batnit.”

notes.text: The compressed genealogy and chronology remain unresolved. Hyman offers two alternatives: changing Shimon son of Rabbi to Shimon, or reading a later descendant of Abba Shaul ben Batnit.

No new primary scalar was returned. Hyman calls Batnit a grandson and then quotes a SON chain; the tension is retained without an extra inferred generation. His two alternatives retain their force: SHOULD READ R’ Shimon rather than Shimon son of Rabbi, OR SHOULD READ of the descendants of Abba Shaul ben Batnit. Neither is admitted as a genealogy. The full רבי within ברבי supports son of Rabbi without identifying him as Yehudah Ha Nasi. The earlier finite Jerusalem Talmud search did not establish absence of Hyman’s passage.

The consulted Mishnah Peah 8:5 calls him Abba Shaul. Beitzah 29a gives the full name Abba Shaul ben Batnit in a separate episode. In the Bavli, the vower is R’ Shimon son of Rabbi (Nedarim 22b), and Batnit son of Abba Shaul ben Batnit proposes an opening (23a). Jerusalem Talmud Nedarim 9:1:6 calls the vower R’ Shimon and gives the role to a Galilean elder, possibly R’ Shimon ben Elazar. The Jerusalem Talmud parallel in Moed Katan 3:1:14 instead calls the vower R’ Shimon son of Rabbi. These versions preserve the differences Hyman discusses and leave his proposed genealogy open.
